title: 2 Fast 2 Surgery: Fast surgery on QLDPC codes with $\tilde{O}(n(k + d))$ space overhead
abstract: We show that the fast surgery framework of Baspin-Berent-Cohen can be instantiated using at most $\tilde{O}(n(k + d))$ ancilla qubits, improving on the previously achievable $O(n\cdot k \cdot d)$ overhead. This result also establishes that fast surgery can be performed at a cost comparable to the $\tilde{O}(nk)$ overhead required for regular surgery. We build the surgery ancilla by first starting with a dense, but expanding system; and then applying expansion-preserving sparsification methods from gauging and code embeddings.
summary: This paper presents a theoretical improvement to the resource overhead required for performing fast surgery on QLDPC codes. By employing advanced techniques from algebraic topology and sparse complex construction, the authors reduce the required ancilla qubits from $	ilde{O}(nkd)$ to $	ilde{O}(n(k+d))$. This advancement is crucial for scaling up fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the space overhead required for performing fast surgery on Quantum Low-Density Parity Check (QLDPC) codes.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that fast surgery can be achieved with a space overhead of $	ilde{O}(n(k+d))$, significantly improving upon previous bounds of $	ilde{O}(nkd)$.
method: The technique involves constructing and sparsifying the surgery ancilla system using algebraic topology tools like mapping cones and leveraging expansion-preserving sparsification methods.
model_or_system: The system under study is QLDPC codes, which are mathematically described using chain complexes ($	ext{C}^{ ullet}$). The process models fault-tolerant quantum computation via code surgery.
key_observables: Space overhead ($	ilde{O}(n(k+d))$), Systole ($	ext{Syst}_i$), and the dimension of the constructed ancilla complex ($\dim 	ext{D}_{	ext{sparse}}^0$).
important_parameters: The code parameters $n$ (physical qubits), $k$ (logical qubits), and $d$ (error threshold).
main_assumptions: The construction relies on defining the dense ancilla using a boosting matrix from random codes, and the final step requires proving the preservation of co-systoles.
paper_structure: The paper builds the surgery ancilla through a sequence of steps: starting with a dense system, applying sparsification via mapping cones, and employing gadgets (like the dual-gauging gadget) to reduce the complexity while preserving key properties like the systole.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the overhead costs associated with fault-tolerant quantum computation, which is a central concern for building large-scale quantum processors.
